principleCandidate.scope: 适用于任何存在易失缓存/会话副本与持久化源文件双轨状态的场景，尤其是跨会话同步、状态合并、心跳任务，以及对外播报/用户可见输出前的最终校验。

principleDraft.title: 持久态为唯一权威：合并与用户可见输出前必须刷新核对源文件
principleDraft.statement: 当同一状态同时存在易失副本（会话记录、内存缓存）与持久化源文件时，必须将最新落盘的持久化状态视为唯一权威：(1) 在任何合并、同步或基于该状态生成用户可见输出/播报之前，必须重新读取源文件，并以源文件内容为基准核对易失副本，冲突时以源文件为准；(2) 不得将易失副本直接当作事实来源；(3) 首次因陈旧副本引发事故后，必须将上述核对固化为显式守卫/检查机制，而非仅修正单次结果。
principleDraft.rationale: 根因是把易失的会话记录当作权威状态，在未核对源文件的情况下合并陈旧内容并送入用户可见的播报链路。将'最新落盘状态'设为唯一事实来源，并在入口（合并/同步）与出口（用户可见输出）两处强制刷新核对，可在两个关口拦截陈旧状态；将核对固化为机制则确保同一失败模式不会重复发生。本原则是 T-03（以可观察证据为准）、T-05（硬约束转显式守卫）、T-10（重要状态须持久化）在'权威来源选择与核对时机'维度上的组合细化。
applicability: 同一状态存在易失副本（会话记录、内存缓存）与持久化源文件双轨表示的场景
跨会话或跨进程的状态同步与合并操作
定时/心跳任务基于状态生成播报内容的链路
任何用户可见输出（播报、报告、通知、状态汇报）前的最终校验
因陈旧副本引发事故后的修复与机制固化
antiPatterns: 将会话记录或内存缓存直接视为权威事实进行合并，而不重读源文件核对
用陈旧易失副本的内容覆盖或混入最新持久化状态
基于未核对的缓存或上下文记忆生成用户可见播报
事故后仅修正本次错误数据，而不把'合并/播报前核对源文件'固化为守卫机制
仅凭上下文记忆断言持久化状态与缓存一致，而不以落盘文件为证据

intentContract.ownerIntent: 当状态同时存在于易失上下文与持久化源文件时，Owner 要求代理永远以最新落盘的源文件为唯一权威，在合并或对外播报前重读核对，绝不允许陈旧的会话/缓存副本被当作事实传播给用户。
intentContract.targetBehavior: 在工具轨迹中可见：每次合并、同步或生成用户可见输出之前，代理都重新读取了持久化源文件，并以源文件为基准核对/修正易失副本，冲突时以源文件为准；事故后的修复包含把该核对固化为可复用的检查或守卫，而不是只改本次数据。
intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: 把易失会话记录或内存缓存当作权威状态，未重读源文件核对就合并陈旧内容并播报给用户；事故后只修正结果而不建立核对机制（同坑摔两次）。
intentContract.evidenceSource: Philosopher 根因诊断：事故源于将易失会话记录当作权威状态，未核对源文件即合并陈旧内容并进入播报链路。
intentContract.validationExpectation: 评估者应核验规则同时包含三要素：(a) 最新落盘持久化状态为唯一权威；(b) 合并与用户可见输出前必须重读并核对源文件；(c) 首次事故后核对必须固化为机制。任何允许缓存直接作为事实、或仅修数据不建机制的改动应被标记为与本意图矛盾。

risks: 与核心公理 T-03（可观察证据）、T-05（硬约束转显式守卫）、T-10（重要状态持久化）部分重叠：本原则是它们在'权威来源选择与核对时机'维度的组合细化，规则生成阶段需去重，避免产出重复规则

以 mtime 判断新鲜度在时钟偏移或文件系统时间粒度较粗时可能失效，落地时应辅以内容或哈希比对
权威性不等于正确性：若源文件本身被错误写入，'以最新持久化为准'会忠实传播错误，还需对源文件写入质量另行校验

principleDraft.title: 持久态为唯一权威：合并与用户可见输出前必须刷新并核对源文件
principleDraft.statement: 当同一状态同时存在易失副本（会话记录、内存缓存）与持久化源文件时，必须以最新落盘的持久化状态为唯一权威：执行任何跨会话同步/心跳合并前，以及产生任何用户可见输出（播报/narration）前，必须重新读取源文件并以 mtime+内容为基准与副本核对；不一致时以源文件为准并回写副本；首次因陈旧副本发生事故后，必须将此核对固化为流程中的显式核对门，而非仅纠正本次结果。
principleDraft.rationale: 根因是同步机制把易失会话记录当作权威状态，在未核对源文件的情况下将陈旧内容合并（12:00 心跳将 08:12 陈旧信任版主题合并入 CURRENT_FOCUS v48）并送入播报链路（19:08 播报致用户二次纠正，而 narration_lines_ep002.json 08:24 已更新）。将最新落盘状态设为唯一事实来源，并在合并入口与用户可见输出出口双重强制刷新核对，可在两端拦截陈旧状态；首次事故后把核对固化为机制而非只改结果，才能阻断同一坑摔两次。
applicability: 跨会话状态同步与心跳合并（触发场景：心跳|同步|merge|合并|CURRENT_FOCUS）
用户可见输出/播报前的最终校验（触发场景：播报|narration_lines）
任何存在易失副本（会话记录、缓存）与持久化源文件双轨表示的关键中间状态（如 CURRENT_FOCUS、narration_lines_ep002.json）
antiPatterns: 以易失会话记录/内存缓存为权威直接执行合并或播报，全程不读取源文件
仅凭 mtime 判断新鲜度而不做内容比对（时钟偏移或文件系统时间粒度粗时失效）
发现副本滞后后仅手工纠正本次结果，不将核对门固化进同步/播报流程，导致同类错误重复发生
把缓存命中或会话记忆当作事实来源，替代源文件证据

intentContract.ownerIntent: Owner 要求跨会话同步与播报以已落盘源文件的 mtime+内容为权威基准，杜绝陈旧会话记录被重复合并与播报导致的用户二次纠正。
intentContract.targetBehavior: 在工具轨迹中可见：任何心跳/同步/合并或播报动作执行前，agent 先读取源文件 mtime 与内容并与易失副本比对，不一致时以源文件为准回写副本后才继续；首次事故后将该核对固化为流程中的显式核对门。
intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: 以易失会话记录或缓存为权威，未经源文件 mtime+内容核对即合并状态或对外播报，且首次事故后仍不把核对固化为机制，导致同一坑摔两次。

intentContract.validationExpectation: 评估者应确认生成的规则在（心跳|同步|merge|CURRENT_FOCUS|播报|narration_lines）触发下强制'先读源文件 mtime+内容并比对，不一致时以源文件为准回写副本'的步骤，并包含首次事故后将核对固化为流程门的要求；任何允许'仅信会话记录'或'仅凭 mtime 不做内容比对'的规则均违背此意图，应被拒绝。

risks: 与核心公理 T-10（重要状态持久化）、T-03（以可观察证据为准）、T-05（硬约束转显式守卫）、T-08 存在部分重叠，本原则是对它们在'权威来源选择与核对时机'维度上的组合细化，下游规则立项需去重，避免重复约束

parsed.thesis: Volatile session memory is a cache, never an authority: every action that propagates internal state into authoritative or user-facing artifacts must first re-verify freshness and content against the durable source of truth, and should remain reversible until that verification passes. The recurring failure was not a single bad merge or broadcast, but the absence of a mandatory freshness gate at each propagation point, allowing stale snapshots to contaminate authoritative work across session boundaries.

principleCandidate.title: Re-verify volatile state against the durable source before any merge or broadcast
principleCandidate.rationale: The root cause was treating in-session snapshots as authoritative, so stale state flowed into CURRENT_FOCUS and user-facing narration without any freshness check. A forced mtime+content comparison against the persistent source at every propagation point (merge, sync, broadcast) blocks both temporal and content staleness at the source, prevents cross-session regression, and—if the check fails—defers the action rather than propagating error.
principleCandidate.scope: Applies whenever internal, cached, or recalled state is about to be merged into authoritative artifacts, broadcast to users, or used as the basis for consequential decisions—especially across session or process boundaries where context was rehydrated from transient memory.

risks: Overlaps partially with existing core axioms: T-03 (observable evidence over inference), T-07 (verify after acting), and T-10 (persist state when continuity matters); the distinct contribution is the mandatory pre-propagation freshness gate on volatile state, but reviewers may consider it derivative
Re-reading and diffing source files at every propagation point adds latency and cost; over-application to high-frequency, low-stakes actions could cause unnecessary thrashing

principleDraft.title: Verify volatile state against the durable source before any merge or broadcast
principleDraft.statement: Before cached, recalled, or rehydrated in-session state is merged into an authoritative artifact, broadcast or narrated to a user, or used as the basis for a consequential decision, the agent must re-read the durable source of truth and compare both freshness (e.g., modification time) and content against the in-memory snapshot. If the snapshot is stale or divergent, the agent must refresh from the source or defer the propagation rather than push the stale state, and must keep the propagation reversible until the verification passes.
principleDraft.rationale: The diagnosed root cause was not a single bad merge but the absence of a mandatory freshness gate at each propagation point: in-session snapshots were treated as authoritative, so stale state flowed into CURRENT_FOCUS and user-facing narration across session boundaries without any check. Forcing a pre-propagation mtime+content comparison against the persistent source blocks both temporal and content staleness at the source, prevents cross-session regression, and converts a would-be silent contamination into a defer-or-refresh decision.
applicability: Merging, syncing, or writing cached or recalled in-session state into authoritative artifacts (e.g., CURRENT_FOCUS, task ledgers, records of decision)
Broadcasting or narrating internal state to users (status updates, summaries, reports) when derived from session memory
Using rehydrated context as the basis for consequential decisions after crossing a session or process boundary
Any propagation point where transient memory is about to become durable or user-visible state
antiPatterns: Treating volatile session memory as authoritative and merging it without re-reading the durable source
Broadcasting user-facing content derived from a stale in-session snapshot with no freshness or content check
Trusting rehydrated context across a session boundary as current without an mtime+content comparison
Proceeding with a merge or broadcast when the freshness check fails, instead of refreshing from the source or deferring the action
Skipping the verification gate for speed on frequent actions that still touch authoritative or user-facing state

intentContract.ownerIntent: The Owner wants to prevent stale in-session snapshots from contaminating authoritative artifacts or user-facing output: volatile session memory must be treated as a cache that is re-verified against the durable source of truth before it is merged, synced, or broadcast.
intentContract.targetBehavior: Immediately before each merge, sync, or broadcast of cached or rehydrated state, the agent visibly re-reads the durable source, performs an mtime and content comparison against the in-memory snapshot, and proceeds only if the snapshot is fresh and identical; otherwise it refreshes from the source or defers the action while keeping it reversible.
intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: Propagating volatile in-session state into authoritative artifacts or user-facing narration without a pre-propagation freshness and content check against the durable source — i.e., treating session memory as authority and letting stale snapshots flow unchecked across session boundaries.
intentContract.evidenceSource: The diagnosed incident family in the pri815-G-manual r2 lineage: stale snapshots merged into CURRENT_FOCUS and emitted in user-facing narration after context rehydration, with no freshness gate at any propagation point (dreamer and philosopher artifacts for this task).
intentContract.validationExpectation: An evaluator should require that any rule generated from this principle mandates an observable pre-propagation re-read plus mtime/content comparison against a named durable source, with explicit refresh-or-defer behavior on check failure and reversibility preserved until verification passes; a rule that permits merging cached state without that gate, or that only verifies after propagation, contradicts this intent and must be flagged.

risks: Partial overlap with core axioms T-03 (observable evidence before inference), T-07 (verify after acting), and T-10 (persist state when continuity matters); the distinct contribution is the mandatory PRE-propagation freshness gate on volatile state, but reviewers may judge the draft derivative of existing axioms
Re-reading and diffing the durable source at every propagation point adds latency and cost; over-application to high-frequency, low-stakes internal updates could cause unnecessary thrashing
Assumes a single, unambiguous durable source of truth exists; with multiple candidate sources the verification may compare against the wrong authority and pass while still propagating divergent state

Strict gating can stall time-critical actions if the verification mechanism or source file is unavailable; no fallback policy for source unavailability is defined, trading correctness for responsiveness
Ambiguity in what counts as a propagation point (authoritative write vs. internal read vs. casual mention) may cause either over-triggering of the gate or missed gates at genuine propagation points

parsed.thesis: Transient working memory is a cache, never an authority. When state loaded into volatile context is about to be used for a consequential action—merging, broadcasting, or handing off across a session boundary—it must be revalidated against its durable, observable source at the moment of use, and divergence must be treated as a blocking condition rather than a hint. Corrections that arise from staleness failures should crystallize into standing checks attached to the trigger points where the failure occurred, so the lesson enforces itself instead of relying on memory.

principleDraft.title: Re-verify volatile state against the authoritative persistent source before consequential use
principleDraft.statement: Whenever state held in volatile working memory (session context, in-memory cache, or a loaded copy) is about to drive a consequential action—cross-session merge, external broadcast, persistent state update, or handoff—the agent must re-read the durable source and compare it against the in-memory copy immediately before the action. The persisted source is the single authority; divergence detected by content comparison (not mtime alone) is a blocking condition requiring reconciliation before proceeding, and if the durable source is unreachable the agent must halt and alert rather than act on the stale copy. When a staleness failure does occur, the correction must be persisted as a standing pre-flight check attached to the trigger point where the failure happened, not retained as informal memory.
principleDraft.rationale: The diagnosed root cause is treating in-session memory as authoritative when a durable source exists, allowing stale state to flow unchecked into merges and external broadcasts and forcing repeated user correction. Declaring the persisted source the single authority and inserting a mandatory compare-and-block step immediately before each consequential action structurally intercepts staleness before it causes external impact, and crystallizing the resulting correction into a standing gate at the trigger point makes the lesson self-enforcing instead of dependent on memory.
applicability: State loaded into volatile context will be used in a cross-session merge, external broadcast, persistent state update, or handoff across a session boundary
Time gaps, multiple writers, or prior user corrections exist between when state was loaded and when it is used
Cross-session resumption where in-memory state may not reflect the durable store
Explicitly out of scope: trivial, read-only, or purely internal operations where staleness is harmless
antiPatterns: Treating in-session memory as authoritative and acting on it without checking the durable source
Merging, broadcasting, or handing off a stale in-memory copy without a fresh pre-use comparison
Treating detected divergence as a non-blocking hint and proceeding anyway
Relying on mtime or other freshness metadata alone without content comparison
Fixing a staleness failure once and relying on informal memory to avoid repeating it, instead of persisting a standing check at the trigger point
Proceeding on a stale copy because the durable source is temporarily unreachable

intentContract.ownerIntent: The Owner wants the agent to never merge, broadcast, persist, or hand off state straight from in-session memory without first re-reading the durable source and halting on any mismatch, so stale data never reaches external or persistent surfaces.
intentContract.targetBehavior: Immediately before each consequential use (merge, external broadcast, persistent write, cross-session handoff), the agent re-reads the durable source, compares its content to the in-memory copy, proceeds only on a match, and otherwise halts and reports the divergence; after a staleness failure it persists a standing pre-flight check at that trigger point.
intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: Acting on volatile in-memory state as if it were authoritative—merging, broadcasting, writing, or handing off a copy without a fresh source comparison, proceeding past detected divergence, trusting mtime alone, or continuing on stale data when the source is unreachable.
intentContract.evidenceSource: The dreamer/philosopher diagnosis of five staleness failure candidates where state held in volatile working memory flowed unchecked into cross-session merges and external broadcasts, forcing repeated user corrections (philosopher artifact pi-art-philosopher-pri815-G-manual_1788612956754_9aa-r3-run1).
intentContract.validationExpectation: An evaluator should accept a rule only if it (a) mandates a durable-source re-read with content comparison immediately before merge/broadcast/persistent-write/handoff actions, (b) makes divergence a blocking halt rather than a warning, (c) requires content comparison rather than mtime alone, (d) specifies halt-and-alert behavior when the source is unreachable, and (e) excludes low-stakes internal reads from the gate.

risks: Overlaps with core axioms T-03 (observable evidence before claims) and T-10 (persist important state); this principle narrows both into source-precedence and pre-use revalidation rather than contradicting them, but downstream consolidation should be considered, and it also composes T-08's feedback-crystallization intent.
Mandatory reload-and-compare before every consequential action adds latency and redundant reads; scope must remain limited to consequential actions and exclude low-stakes internal reads.
A hard block when the durable source is transiently unavailable could stall workflows; the gate needs a defined halt-and-alert fallback rather than deadlocking or silently proceeding.
Freshness signals like mtime are unreliable (coarse granularity, clock skew); if rules implement only metadata checks, the gate can produce false confidence without content comparison.
Over-application risk: treating all in-memory state as suspect may cause excessive conservatism and inhibit fluid operation where reconciliation is genuinely unnecessary.

Divergence handling is deliberately blocking but prescribes no merge-resolution policy; when both copies contain legitimate concurrent changes, escalation to the owner must occur rather than silent resolution, which downstream rule generation must not bypass.

principleDraft.title: Revalidate volatile state against the authoritative source file before consequential use
principleDraft.statement: State loaded into volatile working memory is a cache, never an authority: immediately before any consequential action that consumes cross-session state (merge, heartbeat sync, external broadcast, or session handoff), re-read the authoritative persistent source file and compare both mtime and content against the in-session copy; on any divergence (source newer or content differs), block the action, alert, and refresh state from the source before proceeding. A correction arising from a staleness failure must be crystallized into a standing check bound to the trigger pattern (heartbeat, sync, merge, broadcast) where the failure occurred.
principleDraft.rationale: The diagnosed root cause is a design flaw in which cross-session sync treated session records as authoritative and lacked a source-file mtime+content consistency gate, so stale state flowed unchecked into merges and external broadcasts: on 09-05 the 12:00 heartbeat merged the 08:12 stale trust-version theme into CURRENT_FOCUS v48, and the 19:08 broadcast used stale narration_lines even though narration_lines_ep002.json had already been updated at 08:24, forcing the Owner to correct the same pit twice in one day. Declaring the persisted source file (mtime + content) the single authority and mandating a compare-and-block gate at the moment of consequential use intercepts staleness before external impact, and binding crystallized checks to the failure's trigger points makes the lesson self-enforcing rather than dependent on memory.
applicability: Cross-session merges and heartbeat syncs that write persistent state (e.g., CURRENT_FOCUS version updates)
External broadcasts or announcements derived from previously loaded content (e.g., narration_lines_ep002.json)
State handoffs across session boundaries where time gaps, multiple writers, or a prior correction exist between load and use
Consequential writes or external outputs consuming state loaded earlier into volatile working memory
antiPatterns: Merging or broadcasting state taken directly from in-session memory without re-reading the durable source file first
Proceeding on detected source/session divergence and treating divergence as a non-blocking hint
Declaring freshness from mtime alone (or content alone) without comparing both against the source file
Re-absorbing a staleness correction as one-off context instead of a standing check bound to the trigger point where the failure occurred

intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: Using volatile in-session memory as the authority for a merge, sync, or broadcast without re-validating against the durable source, or proceeding past a detected source/session divergence instead of blocking on it.
